name: Shoulder press
cue: Keep your ribs down and press up and slightly in.
research: research.json biomech.shoulder_press: seated against a back pad reclined ~10 deg (through the thorax_back and sacrum landmarks, 8 deg), hips 82 (trunk-relative 80), knees 90, feet flat. A: humerus 75 deg elevated in the plane 30 deg forward of the frontal plane (scapular plane), elbow ~105, forearm vertical (external rotation 80: the front of the humerus faces up), handles at ear level. B: soft lockout, elevation ~166 (research 160), elbow ~12 (research 10), hands above the crown; scapulohumeral rhythm (BRIEF 2, about 2:1 beyond 30 deg): the shoulder girdle proxy (clavicle elevation, which in this rig stands for scapular upward rotation) ramps 6 -> 22 deg with the press, so of the ~160 deg of read-back humeral elevation about 22 comes from the girdle. The exact 2:1 split (about 45 deg of scapular rotation at 165 deg of elevation) cannot be drawn with this rig: its only girdle degree of freedom is clavicle elevation about the SC joint, which lifts the shoulder joint straight up (about 7 cm at 28 deg, 12 cm at 45) and reads as the hard shrug the research lists as a mistake; about 22 deg is the most it shows as upward rotation without a visible shrug (front view checked). So the drawn split is about 5:1 beyond 30 deg; a true 2:1 needs a scapula bone that rotates about the AC joint (engine change, owner call). The protraction stays near -8 -> -9 (a retracted, elevated girdle pressed the scapulae into the back pad). A girdle ramp authored in the keys rather than the engine rhythm, because the handle path has to be refitted for the higher shoulders: tools/design/shoulder_press_v3.mjs keeps the thorax-frame humerus and forearm of v2 at A and B (read-back elevation 75.5 -> 165.5, elbow 107 -> 13), moves both FK grips with their shoulders and searches the lever hinge again (forearm tilt <= 10.4 deg sideways). Handles on swing levers hinged behind the back pad (hub at head height, 12 cm behind the pad; tools/design/shoulder_press_v2.mjs): with mid keys M1-M3 that bring the elbows 6-10 deg further forward mid-press, the forearms stay under the handles (engine: -8.5 .. +7.7 deg sideways, <= 11 deg fore-aft); the lever stops at -40.8 deg for the soft lockout. The path converges up and slightly back, and the levers stay behind the head and above the shoulders. Overhand grip, palms forward (hand pro picks that side of the handle). Humeral rotation: while the elbow is bent, the vertical forearm under the handle fixes the elbow swivel, so the front of the humerus turns from facing up (start) to facing the head (~150 deg). At the soft lockout the elbows point out and back and the elbow creases face forward-medial, as in a real palms-forward lockout: the B and M3 arm planes (0 and 40.5) only steer the IK pole, and the humerus turns ~60 deg inward over the last fifth of the press (back out early in the lowering) while the forearm supinates to keep the palms forward (measured forearm rotation 125 deg pronation at the bottom, 34 at lockout; range 0-160). Read-back plane stays 21-38 deg below 150 deg of elevation. Without this the front delts sat edge-on in the fold between the raised arm and the neck at the peak (66 ember px at 540); now they face the camera (375 px at 540, 1236 on the phone). Only the front delts glow (research primary). The front delt has its own patch (group delt_front: lateral third of the clavicle over the front of the humeral head to the deltoid tuberosity), which allows a skin bind late in the press (motion.bind 0.74 s into the 1 s press, the arms ~159 deg up) without drips: on the 390x481 phone stage the front-delt glow is ~440 CSS px at the start, ~410 at the peak and ~180-235 mid-press and mid-lowering (loop phases 0.17 / 0.5-0.58 of the earlier 3.7 s loop; 140-200 with an earlier bind, 110-150 with the shared patch and bind 0). It is still smallest mid-press, where the raised arms hide the near cap from any camera inside the 30 deg budget (az 5-35, el 7-26 measured: 95-180 px mid-lowering). Load: a selectorized weight stack behind the back posts; cables from its cap pulley to the lever hubs lift it 0.1 H over the press. (tools/design/loads.mjs)

camera.note: Research view az 30 / el -3 (front three-quarter: vertical forearms, elbows under the handles, the press in the scapular plane). Raised 29 deg and turned 5 deg toward the front (az 25 / el 26, 29 deg in all): the front delts face up at the bottom and forward at the lockout, and looking down onto the shoulder caps lets them read at phone size; from el -3 they are thin slivers under the arms. The floor plate spans only the seat, the posts and the feet, so the horizon arc shows on both sides; the lever arms and hubs use the quiet plate material so they never catch a highlight brighter than the figure's rim.
